evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate only verifies positive changed manager PIDs and nonempty changed invocation IDs; it never requires the manager before/after snapshots to share a nonempty guest boot ID. The separate boot_id_changed check covers only reboot.before/reboot.after. A guest reboot during the manager phase can therefore satisfy manager_restarted, and a later reboot can satisfy boot_id_changed, allowing the feasibility check to pass without proving a manager-only restart. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs on both sides of the manager restart is the smallest compatible correctness fix.
